text: DISCHARGE SUMMARY CHIEF COMPLAINT: Severe retrosternal burning and nocturnal regurgitation. HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS: A 51-year-old female with essential hypertension presents with intractable heartburn and regurgitation exacerbated by lying flat. DIAGNOSTICS: Upper endoscopy showed non-erosive gastro-esophageal reflux disease without esophagitis. HOSPITAL COURSE: Patient responded promptly to high-dose proton pump inhibitor therapy (pantoprazole 40 mg twice daily). Lifestyle modifications and dietary advice reviewed. DISCHARGE DIAGNOSES: 1. Gastro-esophageal reflux disease without esophagitis. 2. Essential (primary) hypertension.

DISCHARGE SUMMARY CHIEF COMPLAINT: Dyspnea, purulent sputum, and pleuritic chest pain. HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS: A 62-year-old male with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and type 2 diabetes presents with acute fever, chills, and dense left lower lobe infiltrate on chest radiograph. PHYSICAL EXAM: Temperature 38.9C, SpO2 89% requiring 3L nasal cannula. Bronchial breath sounds and inspiratory crackles over left base. COURSE: Treated with IV levofloxacin for community-acquired bacterial pneumonia and systemic steroids for acute COPD flare. Discharged in stable condition. DISCHARGE DIAGNOSES: 1. Pneumonia, unspecified organism. 2. Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease with acute exacerbation. 3. Type 2 diabetes mellitus without complications.
